newsitem.title: UK: Germany short of Eurofighter funds - parliamentarian.
newsitem.headline: Germany short of Eurofighter funds - parliamentarian.

text.p: Germany will have a struggle to afford its contributions to the four-country project to build a Eurofighter aircraft for their air forces, the chairman of the German parliament's defence committee said on Sunday.
But because it needs the fighter aircraft militarily and wants to cooperate with its partners, it will have to find the money, said Klaus Rose.
Rose was speaking in an interview to be shown on a BBC television programme which begins at 1920 GMT. The BBC issued a partial text of his remarks in advance of the programme being shown.
"We are in a difficult financial situation in Germany so from this point of view we perhaps could not afford it," Rose said.
"But I think as we need it from the military point of view and as it is a quadrilateral cooperation, we have to."
The Eurofighter is due to be built by a consortium linking British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler Aerospace, Alenia SpA of Italy and Spain's CASA.
Germany has said it will buy some 180 planes to replace those now operated by its airforce.
"The first delivery (to Germany) will perhaps be in 2001 or 2002," Rose forecast, "and the delivery of the last aircraft will be in 2012 or even 2015."
